title: Frazier's favorites Red Happy and James Willigan; Black Benny
summary: Frazier says he came after these drummers, favored Happy and Willigan, who sent him on jobs, and mentions Black Benny.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I used to look at some of them and play. But my two favorite drummers was, in them days was Happy.
Yeah. I used to do lots of releases. After Willigan, he was playing drum. Mm-hmm. And he started wanting to send me on different jobs. Yeah. He liked the way I played, yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
Well, what kind of stuff did he play, James Willigan?

He was a drummer. He used to use plenty of roles. Like I said, the same, almost the same beats like Red Happy, James. Yeah. Want me to make some of them beats he makes? Yeah, sure. Yeah, beats he had to beat something like this.
Oh, yeah. Hey, would he use that on every tune, like Red Happy would use it?

Yeah, well, I figure some of them on most of every tune. You see, on exception of a slow number, well, a drummer, sometimes he's had it. Slow numbers always was hard on a man playing them. Yeah, yeah. Playing the drums. So when you get it, we used to call them bluesy tempos. Yeah, yeah. The day they called it, they got new names for them. We called them bluesy tempos. Well, I figure he played like I played them them days. Falling by honey, starlight. We played something like this. It's not too much of a flag to it. Oh, yeah. Well, one day. We had another one, too, with another fast drummer. It was called Black Benny.

I never know if Black Benny's right, full name, but I know he's played trap drums. We call them trap drums. It's orchestra drumming, and he was a bass drum player in the different brass bands around the city.
